body: Long run, Indian index returns track earnings growth plus dividends plus valuation change. Data points: Marcellus estimates Nifty 50 EPS grew ~10% CAGR over FY05-FY25, with an unusual 24% CAGR over FY21-24 (post-Covid, bank/NBFC cleanup, commodity margins) slowing to ~6% in FY25; Business Standard (May 2025) reported Q4FY25 Nifty EPS growth of just 4.7%, slowest since 2017, and index EPS rising from Rs503 (Mar-2021) to ~Rs1,071. Price return Jun-2005 to Jun-2025: Nifty 2,220.6 to 25,517, ~12.98% CAGR (BacktestIndia) - i.e., ~2-3 points a year of P/E expansion on top of ~10% EPS growth (our arithmetic; NSE also switched from standalone to consolidated earnings for P/E in 2021, which complicates the P/E series). Nifty 50 TR since Nov-1995 is 12.15% (NSE factsheet, 30 Oct 2026); Finnovate computes that by FY26 the 20-year rolling Nifty CAGR dropped below 10% for only the second time, and from the Jan-2008 peak the CAGR to end-FY26 was ~7.3%. Trailing P/E ~19.3-20.7 in Oct 2026 vs ~23-24 a year earlier. Lessons: (1) budget 10-12% nominal index returns, not 15%; (2) starting from high P/Es (2008, 2021, 2024) produced subpar multi-year returns - the same valuation-return link Marks shows for the S&P; (3) earnings growth bursts (2003-08, 2021-24) do the heavy lifting. Actionable: decompose any stock's expected return into EPS growth + dividend yield + P/E change, and refuse theses that need P/E expansion from already-high levels.
title: Nifty earnings vs index returns: ~10% EPS CAGR (FY05-25) vs ~13% price CAGR - the gap was re-rating; FY26 20-yr CAGR fell below 10%
